subject: mainnet canary 2026-09-13
purpose: The primary record (canary-report.json) reports 2 of 52 assertions as FAILED. Those failures
are preserved verbatim and are NOT rewritten to pass. This file is a separate, additive
reconciliation explaining what each failure meant and what the evidence actually shows.
An assertion that was wrong is corrected HERE; the record of it having failed stays THERE.

rootCause.summary: Both assertions encoded a false premise: that we would be the pool's only trader.

event.description: An unrelated address bought CANARY from the public pool 5 blocks after launch.
explicitlyNotEvidenceOf: a real creator or trader validating the product
anything about whether a human would choose to use this
interpretation: The pool is permissionless, so anyone or anything may trade it the moment it exists.
This was almost certainly automated: a launch-sniping bot reacting to a new v4 pool.
It proves the pool is REACHABLE and that fee capture works on volume we did not create.
It proves NOTHING about demand, and must never be cited as user validation.

failedAssertions.originalLabel: every unit is locked liquidity or burned
why: The assertion required pool + burned == totalSupply, which is only true while no token has
ever left the pool. 795.456757 CANARY had already been bought by the third party above.
Supply was never lost or unaccounted; it was held by a trader the assertion did not model.
failedAssertions.correctInvariant: lockedInPool + burned + sum(all discovered holders) == totalSupply
failedAssertions.fixedIn: scripts/lib/launchVerifier.cjs discovers holders from Transfer logs rather than assuming them.
failedAssertions.regressionTest: test/fork/VerifyLaunch.fork.test.js — 'a third party trades BEFORE we verify'

failedAssertions.originalLabel: LP fee is within 1 wei of nominal 25 bps
why: The assertion compared the TOTAL collected LP fee against 25 bps of OUR buy alone.
collectFees settles the position's accrued fees from every trade, not only ours.
The excess is exactly 25 bps of the third party's volume, so the pool charged correctly.
failedAssertions.fixedIn: The verifier reconciles fees against ALL collected events and never against a single assumed trade.

unaffectedFindings: The 50 / 30 / 20 split applied correctly to the third party's fee as well as ours.
All three parties withdrew exactly what they were owed; unaccountedBalance was 0.
Liquidity remained permanently locked throughout; the position is owned by Uniswap's FeeSplitter.

operationalFailures.description: Base fee rose between fee estimation and transaction send.
operationalFailures.error: max fee per gas less than block base fee: maxFeePerGas: 117700593, baseFee: 131992000
operationalFailures.impact: Run aborted mid Phase 1. One funding transfer had landed.
operationalFailures.fixedIn: scripts/lib/canaryPlan.cjs capFor() — explicit cap from the live base fee.
operationalFailures.regressionTest: test/product/CanaryPlan.test.js — 'base fee rose between estimation and send'

operationalFailures.description: Signing wallet funded at the expected price could not afford its own transaction, because a node computes gas allowance as balance / maxFeePerGas.
operationalFailures.impact: Run aborted at Phase 4. Stack and pad were already deployed.
operationalFailures.fixedIn: scripts/lib/canaryPlan.cjs fundingAmountFor() — funds at the cap with headroom.
operationalFailures.regressionTest: test/product/CanaryPlan.test.js — 'signer could not afford its own transaction under maxFeePerGas'

operationalFailures.description: An interrupted run had no resume path and would have redeployed a second stack.
operationalFailures.impact: Potential duplicate contracts and wasted ETH; avoided by adding resume before re-running.
operationalFailures.fixedIn: scripts/lib/canaryPlan.cjs resumePlan() plus attach-instead-of-deploy in canaryExecute.cjs. A PARTIAL stack is refused outright.
operationalFailures.regressionTest: test/product/CanaryPlan.test.js — 'interrupted deployment and partially completed stack'

operationalFailures.description: The budget guard counted phases an interrupted run had already paid for.
operationalFailures.impact: Would have aborted a resumable run as unaffordable.

custody.note: The canary pad-owner and token-creator keys are RETAINED, not rotated or deleted. Their attribution is immutable on chain and they may receive future CANARY fee rewards.

conclusion: No protocol defect was found. Both assertion failures were defects in the canary's own
expectations, and both are now structurally impossible to repeat because the verifier
discovers holders and reconciles fees from events instead of assuming a single trader.
The economic semantics proven on 2026-09-13 are unchanged and are preserved as the baseline.
